definitions.explanation: Having a surface without bumps, curves, or protrusions. Physically flat or level.
Expressed in simple, straightforward terms without complexity or jargon.

examples.japanese: {平|ひら}たい{石|いし}を{拾|ひろ}って{水切|みずき}りをした。
examples.english: I picked up a flat stone and skipped it across the water.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{平|ひら}たい{土地|とち}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This region has a lot of flat land.

examples.japanese: {平|ひら}たい{皿|さら}にケーキを{載|の}せた。
examples.english: I placed the cake on a flat plate.

examples.japanese: {平|ひら}たく{言|い}えば、{失敗|しっぱい}だったということだ。
examples.english: To put it plainly, it was a failure.

examples.japanese: {難|むずか}しい{言葉|ことば}を{使|つか}わずに、{平|ひら}たく{説明|せつめい}してもらえますか。
examples.english: Could you explain it in plain terms without using difficult words?

examples.japanese: {平|ひら}たく{言|い}うと、お{金|かね}が{足|た}りないということです。
examples.english: To put it simply, we don't have enough money.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{平|ひら}たい → {平|ひら}たくない (negative)
・{平|ひら}たい → {平|ひら}たく (adverbial form)
・{平|ひら}たい → {平|ひら}たかった (past)

USAGE:
Sense 1 describes physical flatness:
・{平|ひら}たい{皿|さら} (flat plate)
・{平|ひら}たい{屋根|やね} (flat roof)
・{平|ひら}たい{顔|かお} (flat face)

Sense 2 is used in the expression {平|ひら}たく{言|い}う (to put it simply/plainly).

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{平|たい}ら - Flat, level (more formal/literary)
・{平坦|へいたん} - Flat, even (often for terrain)
・フラット - Flat (loanword, often for musical pitch or design)
